question: to the Commission Leire Pajín (S&D), Hana Jalloul Muro (S&D) Subject:

Lebanon is facing a sharp escalation of violence amid a fragile political transition. In January 2025, Joseph Aoun was elected President, ending more than two years of institutional vacuum. At the same time, Nawaf Salam formed a new government tasked with stabilising the country during a deep economic and political crisis and ongoing tensions between Hezbollah and Israel. The Lebanese authorities have begun a state-led plan to deploy the army in the south and progressively disarm non-state armed groups, although the situation remains highly fragile. In recent days, the situation has deteriorated dramatically. Beirut has reportedly been bombed for the first time since the civil war. More than 600 000 people have been forcibly displaced, an act that constitutes a war crime under the Geneva Conventions. Over 400 people have been killed, including many women and children. 1.
What is the Commission’s assessment of proposals discussed with Arab partners regarding a ceasefire, support for the Lebanese Armed Forces and negotiations between Lebanon and Israel?
How does the Commission plan to increase humanitarian support for the civilian population and displaced persons in Lebanon?
What diplomatic or restrictive measures does the Commission intend to pursue in response to the escalation of attacks and violations of international law involving both Israel and Hezbollah?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.7.2026) The EU remains deeply concerned by the deterioration of the situation in Lebanon and the dramatic socio-economic and humanitarian consequences of the conflict for the civilian population. The EU has consistently called for a cessation of hostilities, the protection of civilians and full respect for international humanitarian law. The EU considers that the ceasefire agreement brokered by the United States between Lebanon and Israel on 3 June 2026 represents a renewed opportunity to end the conflict and create the conditions for lasting peace and security. The EU has consistently called on all parties to fully respect the ceasefire and to fully implement the UNSCR1 1701, calling for the respect of Lebanon’s sovereignty and territorial integrity by Israel and the disarmament of non-state armed groups, including Hezbollah. The EU stands ready to support the Lebanese Government and to contribute to an agreement between Lebanon and Israel, and to supporting the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) to ensure the state's monopoly over the legitimate use of force across Lebanese territory. The European Peace Facility assistance measure2 will directly contribute to reinforcing the operational capacities of the LAF. To address the crisis, the Commission announced3 a package of EUR 100 million humanitarian assistance to Lebanon, targeting all vulnerable populations, including refugees, vulnerable Lebanese and those internally displaced by the conflict, both inside and outside collective shelters. The EU reiterates its strong support for the role of the UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) and condemns all attacks against UN personnel. A continued UN presence in the post-UNIFIL context is essential to ensure the implementation of UNSCR 17014.
1 United Nations Security Council Resolution. 2 Measure of EUR 100 million adopted on 4 June 2026. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-
